title: OOMKilled Pod Recovery
steps: Check pod memory requests/limits: kubectl describe pod <pod-name>
Review recent deployments for memory regression: kubectl rollout history deployment/payment-api
Temporarily increase memory limit: kubectl set resources deployment/payment-api --limits=memory=2Gi
If spike is sustained, scale horizontally: kubectl scale deployment/payment-api --replicas=6

title: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
steps: Check active DB connections: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='active'
Identify long-running queries: SELECT pid, query, query_start FROM pg_stat_activity ORDER BY query_start
Kill blocking queries if needed: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE now() - query_start > interval '5 minutes'
Increase pool size in config: PGPOOL_MAX_CONNECTIONS=50 and restart service

title: Circuit Breaker Open — Cascading Failure
steps: Identify which downstream service triggered the open state in service mesh dashboard
If billing-service is recovering, wait for circuit half-open state (default: 60s)
If sustained, route payment-api to fallback: kubectl set env deployment/payment-api BILLING_FALLBACK=true
